DVA.name: DaVita Inc.
DVA.floating_rate_source: 10-K FY2025, Note 12 Long-term debt: debt table p. F-26, unhedged balance p. F-28 [DEBT ¶61], cap table p. F-29 [DEBT ¶73, ¶95-¶100]; Item 7A p. 69 [7A ¶5]
DVA.floating_rate_basis: Floating debt is Term Loan A-2 $2,000,000k + Term Loan B-2 $1,868,559k (SOFR + margin). Interest rate caps cover $3,500,000k of it in each year 2025-2028 and $1,000,000k in 2029, so only $368,559k of $10,159,463k debt principal (3.6%) is unhedged. Item 7A agrees: +100bp would cut net income by about $5.3M after caps. Not captured by 3.6%: the caps only pay above their strikes (weighted average 4.32% in 2026 rising to 4.50% in 2029, with 25bp step-ups at end-2026 and end-2027), and cover falls to $1.0B in 2029, inside a 5-year loan. Both are memo risks, not stress inputs.
DVA.floating_rate_quote: The remaining $368,559 outstanding principal balance of Term Loan A-2 is subject to SOFR-based interest rate volatility.
memo_points: Interest rate caps protect only above their strikes: weighted average SOFR strike 4.32% in 2026, 4.46% in 2027, 4.43% in 2028, 4.50% in 2029, with 25bp step-ups at end-2026 and end-2027 [DEBT ¶96, ¶97-¶100].
Cap coverage drops from $3.5B (2025-2028) to $1.0B in 2029, inside the requested 5-year tenor [DEBT ¶95]; management describes the caps as shielding exposure 'through 2029' [7 ¶32].

UNP.floating_rate_quote: Interest rates – At both December 31, 2025, and 2024, we did not have variable-rate debt.

KSS.name: Kohl's Corporation
KSS.floating_rate_basis: All long-term debt is fixed rate. The $1.5B revolver is SOFR-based but undrawn at January 31, 2026 ($290M drawn a year earlier). $425M of 2021 notes carry rating-linked coupon step-ups, already triggered; that is a fixed-rate repricing, not floating exposure.
KSS.floating_rate_quote: All other long-term debt is at fixed interest rates and, therefore, is not affected by changes in interest rates. ... There were no outstanding borrowings under the revolving credit facility as of January 31, 2026.
